context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore is a globally distributed e-commerce platform built on AWS to serve 1 million Monthly Active Users with high availability and stringent regulatory compliance. It provides catalog browsing, secure checkout, personalized recommendations, and reviews while supporting multi-currency transactions and third-party logistics integrations.]

## Key Elements
- Customer (Person)
- Admin / Content Manager (Person)
- Online Bookstore System (Software System)
- Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
- Shipping Provider API (FedEx/UPS)
- Notification Service (SendGrid/AWS SES)
- Tax Calculation Service (Avalara/TaxJar)
- Third-Party Recommendation Engine
- Identity Provider (Auth0/AWS Cognito)

## Relationships
- Customer -> Online Bookstore System: HTTPS (Web/Mobile) for browsing and purchasing
- Online Bookstore System -> Payment Gateway: HTTPS/REST for transaction processing
- Online Bookstore System -> Shipping Provider API: HTTPS/REST for fulfillment and tracking
- Online Bookstore System -> Tax Calculation Service: HTTPS/REST (synchronous) for real-time tax evaluation
- Online Bookstore System -> Recommendation Engine: HTTPS/REST with <200ms timeout for product suggestions
- Online Bookstore System -> Identity Provider: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 for authentication and MFA

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: AWS across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 for global reach and 99.95% uptime
- Ingress & Routing: AWS Route 53 (Anycast DNS) for multi-region traffic management
- Security & Compliance: AWS KMS with regional Customer-Managed Keys (CMK), TLS 1.3, and AWS Secrets Manager
- Asynchronous Processing: AWS SQS for decoupling non-blocking operations like shipping and notifications

## Rationale
[Multi-region AWS deployment with Anycast routing guarantees low latency and high availability for the 1M MAU target. Delegating specialized domains to external providers like IdPs and tax engines reduces core system complexity while maintaining GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security standards.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Scaled-down Amazon-style e-commerce site for physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews.
- Built on AWS across multiple regions to support 1M MAU with sub-2s page loads and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer, Admin / Content Manager.
- **Frontend**: Single Page Application (React) served via Amazon CloudFront (CDN) and S3.
- **Ingress**: Amazon API Gateway with JWT validation.
- **Backend Containers**: Core E-Commerce API (Node.js/Express) and Recommendation & Review Service (Python/FastAPI) running on Amazon ECS (Fargate).
- **Data & Caching**: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) Global Database and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider API, Notification Service, Tax Calculation Service, Third-Party Recommendation Engine, Identity Provider.

## Relationships
- **SPA to API Gateway**: HTTPS/JSON for client requests.
- **API Gateway to Core E-Commerce API**: HTTPS via AWS App Mesh/ECS Service Connect.
- **Core E-Commerce API to Recommendation Service**: gRPC over mTLS.
- **Services to Database/Cache**: TLS 1.3 with AES-256 encryption.
- **Global Routing**: AWS Route 53 latency-based routing with failover.

## Technology Stack
- **React/CloudFront/S3**: Client-side rendering and global CDN for sub-2s page load SLA.
- **Node.js/Express & Python/FastAPI**: Microservices handling business logic and async recommendations.
- **Amazon ECS (Fargate)**: Container orchestration minimizing server management.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database**: Transactional storage with cross-region replication for GDPR data residency.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Write-through session and catalogue caching for persistent carts and low latency.
- **AWS App Mesh / Service Connect**: Automated mTLS and service discovery.
- **AWS KMS & Secrets Manager**: Regional encryption keys and secure credential rotation.

## Rationale
- Containerized microservices on AWS ECS with auto-scaling ensure scalable handling of 1M MAU and high availability.
- Multi-region Aurora databases, strict encryption, and mTLS satisfy GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP security constraints.

Single Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore SPA is a React-based e-commerce storefront delivering high-performance catalog browsing, secure checkout, and personalized recommendations for 1M MAU. It prioritizes sub-2-second 3G page loads, multi-currency support, and strict GDPR/CCPA and OWASP compliance.

## Key Elements
- Routing & View Manager (React Router)
- Catalog & Search Module
- Cart & Checkout Module
- Auth & Session Context
- State Management Layer (Zustand / React Context)
- Analytics & Tracking Wrapper
- Amazon S3 & Amazon CloudFront (CDN) with Lambda@Edge
- Amazon API Gateway

## Relationships
- Routing & View Manager -> Catalog & Search Module & Cart & Checkout Module [In-memory routing]
- Cart & Checkout Module -> State Management Layer [In-memory state sync]
- All Modules -> Analytics & Tracking Wrapper [Async event dispatch]
- All Modules -> Amazon API Gateway [HTTPS/JSON via Axios]
- Customer -> Amazon CloudFront [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React: Component-based UI rendering
- React Router: Client-side routing and lazy-loading for performance
- Zustand / React Context: Lightweight state management for optimistic UI updates
- Amazon S3 & Amazon CloudFront: Global static asset hosting and CDN delivery
- Lambda@Edge: Geo-based currency routing and security headers
- Zod: Client-side input validation and sanitization

## Rationale
This architecture leverages a decoupled SPA hosted on a global CDN to achieve sub-2-second load times on 3G and 99.95% uptime. In-memory token handling, strict CSP headers, and edge security controls ensure robust GDPR/CCPA and OWASP Top-10 compliance.

Amazon API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
- Scalable e-commerce online bookstore serving 1 million Monthly Active Users globally across three AWS regions with 99.95% uptime.
- Provides secure catalog browsing, multi-currency purchasing, customer reviews, and personalized book recommendations.

## Key Elements
- **Client Tier**: Single Page Application (React) hosted on Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3.
- **Edge Security & Routing Tier**: Amazon API Gateway with AWS WAF, featuring Request Validator, Router/Authorizer (JWT), Throttling/Rate Limiting, Transform & Edge Routing, and Edge Caching components.
- **Backend Compute Tier**: Core E-Commerce API and Recommendation & Review Service running on Amazon ECS (Fargate) via AWS App Mesh and ECS Service Connect.
- **Data & Integration Tier**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database, Amazon ElastiCache Redis, Identity Provider, Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider API, and Notification Service.

## Relationships
- Single Page Application -> Amazon API Gateway: Sends client requests [HTTPS/JSON] with TLS 1.3.
- Amazon API Gateway -> Identity Provider: Validates user tokens [OIDC/OAuth 2.0].
- Amazon API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce API: Routes validated, sanitized requests with currency context [HTTPS via AWS App Mesh/ECS Service Connect using mTLS or AWS IAM SigV4].
- Core E-Commerce API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database: Reads and persists transactional data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS].

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Infrastructure**: AWS across regions `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` managed via Terraform/AWS CDK for multi-region resilience.
- **API Management & Security**: Amazon API Gateway, AWS WAF, AWS IAM, and JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for secure, throttled edge routing.
- **Frontend**: React served via Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3.
- **Backend Compute**: Node.js with Express and Python with FastAPI hosted on Amazon ECS (Fargate).
- **Data Stores**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database and Amazon ElastiCache Redis.

## Rationale
- Leverages globally distributed AWS services like Amazon CloudFront, API Gateway Edge Caching, and Aurora Global Databases to guarantee sub-2-second page loads on 3G and 99.95% availability for 1M MAU.
- Integrates AWS WAF, strict IAM/mTLS policies, and API Gateway input validation to meet stringent GDPR/CCPA privacy standards and OWASP Top-10 security requirements.

Core E-Commerce API.analysis:
## Overview
The Core E-Commerce API is a Node.js and Express modular monolith running on Amazon ECS Fargate that manages online bookstore transactions, catalogs, and fulfillment. It provides secure, scalable e-commerce services supporting multi-currency checkout, fast browsing, and global availability.

## Key Elements
- **Catalog Component**: Express Router and pg query builder managing book browsing and keyword search.
- **Cart Management Component**: In-memory session manager handling ephemeral shopping carts and promotional discounts via Amazon ElastiCache.
- **Order & Checkout Component**: Domain service module handling secure checkout, tax calculation, payment processing, and inventory reservation.
- **Fulfillment Component**: Integration adapter managing shipping provider APIs and tracking data.

## Relationships
- **Amazon API Gateway** -> **Core E-Commerce API**: Routes validated HTTP requests using HTTPS via AWS App Mesh.
- **Catalog Component** -> **Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL)** & **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Queries catalog data via TCP/SQL and Redis RESP.
- **Cart Management Component** -> **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Stores session and cart states via Redis RESP.
- **Order & Checkout Component** -> **Tax Calculation Service**, **Payment Gateway**, & **Notification Service**: Communicates via HTTPS/REST.
- **Fulfillment Component** -> **Shipping Provider API**: Manages order fulfillment via HTTPS/REST.

## Technology Stack
- **Node.js & Express**: Core runtime and framework for fast, lightweight routing.
- **Amazon ECS (Fargate)**: Serverless container orchestration for scalable microservice execution.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Relational database for durable transactional data with global replication.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: In-memory cache for sub-millisecond cart retrieval and session management.
- **AWS App Mesh & CodeDeploy**: Handles service mesh networking, canary traffic shifting, and blue/green deployments.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a modular monolith on ECS Fargate to balance operational simplicity with strict domain isolation for cart, catalog, and checkout workflows. Integrating Redis for ephemeral cart state and Aurora for global transactional data ensures sub-2-second page loads and 99.95% availability under high concurrent load.

Recommendation & Review Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Recommendation & Review Service is a Python-based FastAPI microservice running on AWS ECS Fargate that manages product recommendations and 5-star customer reviews for the Online Bookstore. It ensures high performance, regional scalability, and strict GDPR/CCPA compliance for 1 million monthly active users.

## Key Elements
- API Controller Component (FastAPI)
- Review Management Component
- Recommendation Aggregator Component
- Data Access Repository Component (async SQLAlchemy)
- Caching / Fallback Store Component (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Review Event Consumer Component (Amazon SQS / SNS)
- Third-Party Recommendation Engine (External System)
- Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) Global Database

## Relationships
- Core E-Commerce API -> API Controller: Invokes endpoints [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Controller -> Review Management & Recommendation Aggregator: Delegates operations [In-process]
- Recommendation Aggregator -> Third-Party Recommendation Engine: Fetches product suggestions [HTTPS/REST with circuit breaker]
- Recommendation Aggregator -> Caching / Fallback Store: Reads/writes cached recommendations [Redis TLS]
- Review Management & Recommendation Aggregator -> Data Access Repository: Persists and queries data [Async SQLAlchemy via TLS 1.3]
- Review Management -> Review Event Consumer: Publishes review events [Amazon SQS / SNS]

## Technology Stack
- Python / FastAPI: Lightweight, high-performance framework ideal for asynchronous microservices.
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Serverless container orchestration for multi-region scaling (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`).
- Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) Global Database: Distributed relational storage with multi-region replication.
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Low-latency caching for pre-computed recommendations and heuristics fallback.
- Amazon SQS / SNS: Asynchronous event messaging with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) for review processing.
- Pydantic: Strict input validation and sanitization for OWASP Top-10 and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.95% availability and sub-second performance by decoupling review ingestion via SQS queues and protecting against third-party outages using Redis fallbacks. Strict input validation, encryption, and regional containerization secure user data while supporting 1M MAU globally.

Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) Global Databa.analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon-scale online bookstore providing catalog browsing, shopping carts, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations. The system is architected for global scale, supporting 1 million monthly active users (MAU) with high availability and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer, Admin / Content Manager
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider API, Notification Service, Tax Calculation Service, Third-Party Recommendation Engine, Identity Provider
- **Frontend Container**: Single Page Application (React, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon S3)
- **API & Routing**: Amazon API Gateway (AWS API Gateway, JWT)
- **Backend Services**: Core E-Commerce API (Node.js, Express, Amazon ECS (Fargate)), Recommendation & Review Service (Python, FastAPI, Amazon ECS (Fargate))
- **Database Components**: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL) Global Database, Amazon RDS Proxy, Primary Cluster Instance (Writer), Cross-Region Read Replica Instances, Aurora Storage Volume, PostgreSQL Extension Manager

## Relationships
- Single Page Application -> Amazon API Gateway: HTTPS / REST [TLS 1.3]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Core E-Commerce API: HTTPS / REST [TLS 1.3]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Recommendation & Review Service: HTTPS / REST [TLS 1.3]
- Core E-Commerce API -> RDS Proxy (Primary): PostgreSQL wire protocol [TLS 1.3]
- Recommendation & Review Service -> RDS Proxy (Regional Replicas): PostgreSQL wire protocol [TLS 1.3]
- RDS Proxy -> Primary Cluster Instance (Writer) / Cross-Region Read Replicas: PostgreSQL wire protocol [TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: React hosted on Amazon S3 and delivered via Amazon CloudFront for low-latency global static asset delivery.
- **Compute**: Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate for serverless container orchestration of Node.js and Python microservices.
- **Database & Storage**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database with cross-region replication for low-latency regional reads and data residency.
- **Connection Pooling & Security**: Amazon RDS Proxy for connection management and IAM authentication enforcement.
- **Infrastructure & Monitoring**: Terraform for Infrastructure as Code, AWS CloudWatch, and AWS DevOps Guru for observability.

## Rationale
This multi-region AWS architecture ensures a sub-2-second page load time on 3G networks globally and meets the 99.95% uptime requirement. Utilizing RDS Proxy, read replicas, and isolated compute tasks enables seamless horizontal scalability for 1 million MAU while enforcing strict GDPR/CCPA compliance standards.

Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).analysis:
## Overview
- Defines internal component decomposition and operational safeguards for the Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) container.
- Supports 1M MAU scale, sub-2s page loads, and zero cart data loss for the online bookstore.

## Key Elements
- Redis Cluster Engine (Primary and Replica nodes across multiple Availability Zones)
- Session Store Module (`sess:*` keyspace for encrypted user sessions and shopping carts)
- Catalogue Cache Module (`cat:*` keyspace with LRU eviction for product metadata and search facets)
- Core E-Commerce API (Client interacting via Redis RESP protocol)

## Relationships
- Core E-Commerce API -> Session Store Module (Redis RESP protocol over TLS 1.3) for sub-millisecond cart lookups
- Core E-Commerce API -> Catalogue Cache Module (Redis RESP protocol over TLS 1.3) for read-heavy product metadata

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS / Memory Store): Managed caching engine ensuring high availability and sub-millisecond latency.
- Redis Append-Only File (AOF) & Daily Snapshots: Persistence strategy ensuring zero data loss during failovers.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMK) providing encryption at rest for PII and session data.
- TLS 1.3: In-transit encryption across all shards and connections.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Automatic rotation of Redis AUTH credentials.

## Rationale
- Logical keyspace separation prevents catalog cache thrashing from evicting critical user session data.
- Multi-AZ deployment, AOF persistence, and strict replica write settings guarantee 99.95% uptime and GDPR/CCPA compliance.
